sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Browser-side setup
sections.what: Marks the file to run in the visitor's browser and brings in the React tools it uses.
sections.why: Dragging and pointer tracking only work in the browser, so this file must run on the visitor's side.

sections.name: Slot
sections.title: Window position shape
sections.what: Defines the three numbers that place a window: left, top and width, each as a percent of the stage.
sections.why: Lets each window's place be set with simple numbers that scale with the screen.
sections.watch_out: Values are percentages of the stage, so changing the stage size moves every window.

sections.name: OsWindow (part 1)
sections.title: Drag start and move
sections.what: Lets a visitor drag the window by its title bar on wide screens. Dragging is ignored on small screens, on static windows, and when a button is pressed.
sections.why: Likely reason: small screens have no room for loose windows, so dragging is limited to wide screens.
sections.watch_out: Dragging depends on remembering where the press began; changing the title bar layout can break press detection.

sections.name: OsWindow (part 2)
sections.title: Window frame and content
sections.what: Draws the window frame, title bar with decorative dots, title text, pull-out button and a scrollable body. Each window appears with a short delay based on its position in the sequence.
sections.why: The staggered delay makes the windows open one after another.
sections.watch_out: The body has a height limit that differs on wide screens, so long content scrolls inside the window.

summary: A draggable window frame used in the desktop-style experience layout, with a title bar, optional label, pull-out button and a scrollable content area.
purpose: Gives a card-like window that visitors can move around on wide screens and open into a fuller reading view.
why: Likely reason: the page is styled like a desktop, and the window falls back to normal page flow on small screens and for static windows.
how: 1. The parent passes in the window's starting position, title, content and handlers. 2. On wide screens the window is placed at that position. 3. Pressing the title bar starts a drag, and moving the pointer shifts the window. 4. Releasing the pointer ends the drag. 5. The pull-out button calls the parent's expand action.
inputs: Title, optional meta text, a position (slot), stacking order, focus and expand handlers, an optional dark style, a static flag, and child content.
outputs: A window section on the page. It calls the focus handler when touched and the expand handler when the pull-out button is pressed.
risks: Dragging is only active on wide screens. The drag offset is held in component state and not saved, so a page reload resets positions. Static windows ignore dragging.
debug: If a window sits in the wrong place, check the slot percentages passed by the parent. If dragging does nothing, check the screen width and that the pointer press is not on a button. If the pull-out button fails, check the handler the parent passes in.
